question: Can a small numeric candidate scorer predict useful future routed-expert demand better than cheap causal history, at an affordable runtime cost?
inspiration: Pinned Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev scalar independent candidate decision head; no language backbone or published Jev accuracy reused.
target: log1p total routed entries over next4verify windows, including rejected MTP branches; ranking/count regression, not softmax or independent calibrated probabilities
availability: Features use only observed routing through current window and initial state. Prediction runs after completed verify at every4runtime rounds.
separation: Entire independent task episodes; saved short task texts, not nonce variants of benchmark. No holdout labels used in preprocessing/training/calibration.
models: 16hidden temporal MLP with explicit lag/momentum features
calibration: Affine expected-count calibration on separate calibration episode; no probability claim
finite_budget: One seed per model, maximum600Adam minibatches per MLP, bounded CPU numeric training; no grid. Full causal heldout ranking and finite-transfer replay afterward.
validity: Preprocessing from development only; whole-task labels frozen. Report memory/scoring/feature costs and sampling. Predictor accuracy or offline coverage is not measured TG.
completion: Save datasets/manifests/checkpoints, bounded training/evaluation, temporal disposition and replay against same capacities/transfer constraints. Integrate only justified candidates or document evidenced blocker.
